description.value: The study examined neural responses to food pictures as a function of food availability and caloric density in healthy participants using a 2 × 2 fMRI design, including exploratory moderation by hunger and gender.

spans.text: To examine this question, 32 healthy participants (16 women) underwent functional magnetic resonance imaging while passively viewing available foods – i.e. foods that could be eaten during and after the experiment – and unavailable foods of either high or low-caloric density in a 2 × 2 design.

value: We expected the perception of high-compared to low-caloric food to enhance activity in the orbital and medial PFC, ACC, amygdala, and insula ( ).
Available compared to unavailable foods might recruit the reward system to a stronger degree (i.e. the ventral and dorsal striatum, ).
Importantly, we expected an interaction of caloric value with availability such that high-caloric foods in the available condition are associated with the strongest response in reward coding regions.

spans.text: We expected the perception of high-compared to low-caloric food to enhance activity in the orbital and medial PFC, ACC, amygdala, and insula ( ).

description.value: A cross-sectional 2 × 2 factorial fMRI study of 32 healthy participants, with food availability crossed with caloric density; participants underwent mild food deprivation before scanning.

spans.text: Thus, the present study presented participants with food images under instructions that half of the displayed foods were available during as well as after scanning whereas the other half of foods were unavailable during the whole experiment.
Palatability ratings were submitted to a Calorie (high calorie, low calorie) by Availability (available, not available) repeated measures analysis of variance (ANOVA).
